svg.title: Different experiments reveal different contributions: human stimulation, macaque recordings, and mouse circuit manipulation
svg.desc: Three separate bands. Band A, humans, intervention: two equal site cards, right frontopolar cortex and vertex control, each beside the same figure-eight coil icon labeled cTBS, grouped by a bracket; an arrow leads to a Horizon task icon with a first free choice marked on a one-or-six-choice strip. Results relative to control: directed exploration reduced; random exploration, no detected reduction. Band B, macaques, recordings: a screen with three different illustrative images in a triangle, then, after a new option is introduced, the same screen with one image replaced; the monkey chooses by saccade, with juice or no reward. Two separate study cards, OFC study and ventral striatum / amygdala study, are each linked by a dashed arrowless line to a model card listing immediate expected return and exploration bonus; the key reads association with model variables. Band C, mice, circuit manipulation: vignettes of a mouse sniffing and handling a plain object; a circuit in which prelimbic cortex sends excitatory input to inhibitory neurons in medial zona incerta, which sends an inhibitory projection to lateral periaqueductal gray. At medial ZI, a manipulation marker carries upward and downward triangle symbols labeled activate and inhibit. The result label reads investigation depth changes, and a dashed arrow labeled behavioral effect points to the vignettes. A key distinguishes solid identified connections from the dashed behavioral effect. No arrows cross between bands.
